chief_complaint: Fatigue and a rash on his neck that started as a papule 2 days earlier, associated with significant non-painful swelling and a pressure sensation in the neck.
history_of_present_illness: The lesion began as a papule 2 days prior, associated with non-painful swelling and pressure sensation; patient experienced diaphoresis with mild confusion and headache; recalls a skin break 3 days prior while shaving; initially received one dose of a first-generation cephalosporin and discharged, but returned due to worsening malaise and neck swelling with mild difficulty breathing.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Patient is a postal worker; no insect bite, animal contact, or foreign travel reported; later identified exposure through handling contaminated mail as a postal worker.
vitals: Temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), pulse 118 bpm, blood pressure 138/90 mmHg, and respiratory rate 20 breath cycles per minute.
physical_exam: Examination reveals a 2cm irregularly shaped, indurated non-tender patch on the left anterior neck with mild overlying erythema and several 2 to 3 mm vesicles; the main lesion has a 6 mm shallow ulceration; massive neck oedema making lymph nodes difficult to assess; neck circumference increased from 57cm at baseline to a peak of 81 cm.
labs_and_diagnostics: Full blood count, Na+, K+, Cl¯ HCO3, BUN, creatinine and random glucose were normal except for a mildly elevated haemoglobin at 18.7g/dL; blood cultures initially grew gram-positive rods; Gram stain and culture of skin lesion obtained at second visit were negative for B. anthracis; stains for bacteria and IHC of skin biopsy showed abundant bacilli and B. anthracis antigens; serology revealed antibody to protective antigen in convalescent serum.
differential_diagnosis: Bacterial ecthyma (Streptococcus pyogenes, Staphylococcus aureus), rickettsial diseases, necrotic arachnidism (bite by brown recluse spider), rat-bite fevers (Streptococcus moniliformis and Spirillum minus), ulceroglandular tularaemia, and bubonic plague, with cutaneous anthrax being the most important consideration in the setting of bioterrorism investigation.
management_and_clinical_course: Initially given one dose of a first-generation cephalosporin; later admitted and received intravenous levofloxacin and ampicillin-sulbactam, and recovered; empirical antibacterial treatment with a quinolone or doxycycline is recommended while awaiting microbiological results for limited cutaneous infection.
